text:
The rain beat faster beyond the workshop, and a gust sent a cool spray through the wide gate. Mert remained in the approach, still holding the safety boundary in place. Aya stood inside with him. The restored mosaic panel rested where it had been, fragile and intact.

Aya looked from the panel to the covered yard beyond Mert. Her impatience had not vanished. It showed in her tight jaw and the quick tap of her fingers against her own leg. She seemed ready to argue again, but then she studied the fitted pieces of the mosaic.

If one side dipped, even for a moment, all their work could be ruined.

Aya drew a breath. “Mert, will you help me carry the panel? I mean together, one of us on each side, all the way along the covered route.”

Mert watched her as she asked. He did not interrupt or step away from the gate approach. When she finished, he glanced at the panel and then met her eyes.

“Yes,” he said. “I’ll help you carry it. We’ll keep our hold coordinated and take the route carefully.”

Aya heard his answer and saw that he meant it. Some of the stiffness left her shoulders.

“Good,” she said. “Together, then.”

Neither of them reached for the panel yet. It remained resting in the workshop, untouched and intact. Mert also stayed where he was, so the gate boundary remained active. Outside, the wind drove the strengthening rain across the yard, but the established route still waited under cover.

Aya faced the panel again. Asking had cost her a little pride, but less than breaking something that belonged to everyone.
